description.content: A set of tabs, only one of which is shown at a time.
Distinguishes tabsets from splits.
Uniquely identifies the tabset within the workspace.

Optional in the defaultModel prop and the setModel method; tabsets without ids are assigned ids based on their position (e.g. "tabset-0-1"). Tabsets created by the workspace (e.g. by dropping a tab onto the edge of another tabset) are assigned generated ids.
Size of the tabset within its parent split.

Interpretation rules:

  • Numbers are percentages of the parent split (e.g. size: 25 is 25 percent)
  • Strings may specify other units (e.g. size: "250px"); strings without units are percentages
  • Siblings without a size share the remaining space evenly
String sizes are only initial sizes: they're converted to percentages when the user resizes the split, and (like percentages) they scale with the workspace when it's resized.
Minimum width of the tabset's content area (not including its header). Overrides the Workspace's tabsetMinWidth prop.

Interpretation rules:

  • Strings must specify a unit: "px", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw" (e.g. minWidth: "200px")
  • Percentages (and strings without units) are not allowed
Minimum height of the tabset's content area (not including its header). Overrides the Workspace's tabsetMinHeight prop.

Interpretation rules:

  • Strings must specify a unit: "px", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw" (e.g. minHeight: "200px")
  • Percentages (and strings without units) are not allowed
Where the tabset's tabs are placed relative to its content. Overrides the Workspace's tabPlacement prop.
See the Workspace's tabPlacement prop for how placement affects tabsets.
Tabsets created by the workspace (e.g. by dropping a tab onto the edge of another tabset) use the Workspace's tabPlacement prop.
The tabset isn't removed when its last tab is closed or dragged away; it stays (showing the Workspace's renderEmptyTabset content) until it is closed (see closeTabset).
By default, tabsets without tabs are removed (other than the root tabset of an empty workspace).
Tabsets created by the workspace (e.g. by dropping a tab onto the edge of another tabset) don't keep this flag.
Id of the selected tab.
Application data for the tabset.
Tabsets created by the workspace start without data.
Tabs in the tabset, in the order they are shown.
